title: Gate the UI brief's ork-only render sections by project, and keep a generic TUI route in ui.md for other projects. Both `## CLI text renders` and the new `## TUI renders` are written for every UI brief with no project check (`internal/engine/brief.go:231-238`). `roles_test.go:821-822` says "The UI pass runs in any project". ui.md:65-67 now sends every project's TUI views to that ork-only section, and the generic out-of-tree route is gone. A UI pass on another project would be told to run `go test ./internal/tui -run TestRenderTUIViews`, which does not exist there, and would then render nothing. The spec's step 6 asked for this wording, so the slice is not wrong. The cross-project gap is new. CONFIRMED by reading. PLAUSIBLE as to how often ork runs UI passes on other projects.

sections.body:
Raised by the reviewer in round 1 of ork run ork-20261127-194957-90f9 for S538 (discovered from S538):

Gate the UI brief's ork-only render sections by project, and keep a generic TUI route in ui.md for other projects. Both `## CLI text renders` and the new `## TUI renders` are written for every UI brief with no project check (`internal/engine/brief.go:231-238`). `roles_test.go:821-822` says "The UI pass runs in any project". ui.md:65-67 now sends every project's TUI views to that ork-only section, and the generic out-of-tree route is gone. A UI pass on another project would be told to run `go test ./internal/tui -run TestRenderTUIViews`, which does not exist there, and would then render nothing. The spec's step 6 asked for this wording, so the slice is not wrong. The cross-project gap is new. CONFIRMED by reading. PLAUSIBLE as to how often ork runs UI passes on other projects.
